steps.say: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis is classified by ILAR criteria into seven categories based on clinical features in the first six months of disease in children younger than sixteen years, with symptoms persisting for at least six weeks. Seven buckets from the first half year are what steer eyes, drugs and prognosis.
steps.tx: **Juvenile idiopathic arthritis** (JIA) is classified by the **ILAR** criteria into **seven categories** based on clinical features in the first **6 months** of disease in children younger than **16 years**, with symptoms persisting for at least **6 weeks**. Seven buckets from the first half year are what steer eyes, drugs and prognosis.

steps.say: Oligoarticular JIA affects four or fewer joints during the first six months, predominantly large lower extremity joints such as knee and ankle in young girls. Patients with positive antinuclear antibodies face a twenty to thirty percent risk of asymptomatic chronic bilateral anterior uveitis causing band keratopathy, cataracts and blindness unless detected early by routine scheduled slit-lamp screening. Few joints plus ANA is the rule for eyes on schedule.
steps.tx: **Oligoarticular JIA** affects **4 or fewer joints** during the first 6 months, predominantly large lower extremity joints (knee, ankle) in young girls. Patients with positive **antinuclear antibodies (ANA)** face a **20% to 30%** risk of asymptomatic, chronic, bilateral **anterior uveitis** causing **band keratopathy**, cataracts, and blindness unless detected early by routine scheduled **slit-lamp screening**. Few joints plus ANA is the rule for eyes on schedule.

vis.alt: Asymmetric knee synovitis within four joints with leg overgrowth beside chronic anterior uveitis triad and ANA label.
vis.caption: Few joints with overgrowth beside uveitis triad. Screening rhythm is in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).

steps.say: Systemic JIA is an autoinflammatory disorder characterized by daily quotidian spiking fevers, an evanescent salmon-pink maculopapular rash that surfaces with fever spikes, hepatosplenomegaly, generalized lymphadenopathy, polyserositis, and marked leukocytosis with extreme hyperferritinemia, driven by interleukin one and interleukin six. Daily spikes with rash are systemic disease.
steps.tx: **Systemic JIA** (sJIA) is an **autoinflammatory** disorder characterized by daily **quotidian** spiking fevers, an evanescent **salmon-pink** maculopapular rash that surfaces with fever spikes, hepatosplenomegaly, generalized lymphadenopathy, **polyserositis**, and marked leukocytosis with extreme hyperferritinemia, driven by **IL-1 and IL-6**. Daily spikes with rash are systemic disease.

vis.alt: Knee pannus and effusion beside salmon pink rash torso and anterior uveitis eye in juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
vis.caption: Joint, skin and eye faces of JIA. Fever pattern and cytokines are in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).

steps.say: Macrophage activation syndrome is a life-threatening complication in up to ten percent of systemic JIA patients, classified under secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Diagnostic hallmarks in a febrile patient with confirmed systemic JIA require serum ferritin above six hundred eighty four plus two of: platelet count at or below one hundred eighty one thousand, AST above forty eight, triglycerides above one hundred fifty six, or fibrinogen at or below three hundred sixty. Falling counts amid fever trigger the hunt.
steps.tx: **Macrophage activation syndrome** (MAS) is a life-threatening complication in up to **10%** of systemic JIA patients, classified under secondary **hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis** (sHLH). Diagnostic hallmarks (2016 EULAR/ACR/PRINTO criteria) in a febrile patient with confirmed sJIA require serum ferritin **>684 ng/mL** plus two of: platelet count **<=181,000/microL**, **AST >48 U/L**, triglycerides **>156 mg/dL**, or fibrinogen **<=360 mg/dL**. Falling counts amid fever trigger the hunt.

rows: Ferritin plus any two, in febrile sJIA, up to 10 percent

steps.say: Therapy for systemic JIA with active systemic features prioritizes biological blockade of the interleukin one pathway with anakinra, a recombinant interleukin one receptor antagonist, or canakinumab, a monoclonal anti interleukin one beta antibody, or the interleukin six pathway with tocilizumab, frequently enabling rapid glucocorticoid withdrawal. Block the cytokine, drop the steroids. Steroid-free remission is the aim.
steps.tx: Therapy for systemic JIA with active systemic features prioritizes biological blockade of the **IL-1 pathway** (**anakinra** [recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist], **canakinumab** [monoclonal anti-IL-1beta antibody]) or **IL-6 pathway** (**tocilizumab**), frequently enabling rapid **glucocorticoid withdrawal**. Block the cytokine, drop the steroids. Steroid-free remission is the aim.

steps.say: Enthesitis-related arthritis occurs predominantly in boys older than six years, linked to HLA-B27, presenting with lower extremity asymmetric arthritis and tender enthesitis at the Achilles tendon insertion, plantar fascia and patellar tendon, acute symptomatic unilateral anterior uveitis, and potential progression to axial spondyloarthritis. Insertions, eyes and B27 are what define it.
steps.tx: **Enthesitis-related arthritis** (ERA) occurs predominantly in boys older than **6 years**, linked to **HLA-B27**, presenting with lower extremity asymmetric arthritis and tender **enthesitis** (Achilles tendon insertion, plantar fascia, patellar tendon), acute symptomatic unilateral **anterior uveitis**, and potential progression to **axial spondyloarthritis**. Insertions, eyes and B27 are what define it.

steps.say: Polyarticular JIA involves five or more joints during the first six months. RF-negative polyarticular JIA is heterogeneous, while RF-positive polyarticular JIA resembles adult rheumatoid arthritis, occurs in adolescent girls with shared epitope HLA-DRB1 alleles, and exhibits an aggressive erosive disabling clinical course. Five plus joints with RF positivity is adult-like disease.
steps.tx: **Polyarticular JIA** involves **5 or more joints** during the first 6 months. **RF-negative** polyarticular JIA is heterogeneous, while **RF-positive** polyarticular JIA resembles adult rheumatoid arthritis, occurs in adolescent girls with shared epitope **HLA-DRB1** alleles, and exhibits an aggressive erosive, disabling clinical course. Five plus joints with RF positivity is adult-like disease.

rows: 5 or more joints in first 6 months
Adult-like, adolescent girls, HLA-DRB1, erosive and disabling

steps.say: Active macrophage activation syndrome demands emergency treatment with high-dose intravenous pulse methylprednisolone at thirty milligrams per kilo per day up to one gram per day for three days combined with high-dose anakinra up to eight to ten milligrams per kilo per day or cyclosporine. Refractory cases require etoposide or emapalumab, a monoclonal anti interferon gamma antibody. Storm protocol starts at once.
steps.tx: Active **macrophage activation syndrome** demands emergency treatment with high-dose intravenous pulse **methylprednisolone** (**30 mg/kg/day** up to **1 g/day** for **3 days**) combined with high-dose **anakinra** (up to **8 to 10 mg/kg/day**) or **cyclosporine**. Refractory cases require **etoposide** or **emapalumab** (monoclonal anti-IFN-gamma antibody). Storm protocol starts at once.

vis.alt: Cytokine storm with haemophagocytic macrophages engulfing erythrocytes in macrophage activation syndrome.
vis.caption: Cytokine storm and haemophagocytosis. Pulse and rescue doses are in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).
